questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.

Everyone feels that he is __pompous__, but I know the underlying truth that he is a man of great understanding and love
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Modest**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"pompous"** refers to someone who is overly self-important or arrogant; showing off in an attempt to impress others. (आत्ममुग्ध)
 
 
 
• **Example: **The CEO's pompous speech about his own success left many employees feeling disconnected.
 
 

 
• **"Modest" **refers to someone who does not boast about their abilities or achievements and tends to be unassuming or humble in nature. (विनम्र)
 
 
 
• **Example: **Despite her many achievements, she remained modest and always credited her team for their hard work.
 
 

 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'pompous' **is **'modest'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Modest**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Lofty **(उच्च): Of imposing height; especially impressively high or tall.
 
 
 
• **Example:** The lofty mountains surrounding the village create a breathtaking view.
 
 

 
• **Grandiose **(भव्य ): Impressive or magnificent in appearance or style, especially pretentiously so.

 
 
• **Example: **The billionaire's grandiose mansion was filled with priceless art and lavish decorations.
 
 

 
• **Haughty** (घमंडी): Arrogantly superior and disdainful.

 
 
• **Example:** His haughty demeanor made it difficult for others to approach him with their ideas.

questions.question:
Select the grammatically correct version of the following sentence.

He was youngest than his brother.

options.text: He was younger than his brother.
He was youngest to his brother.
He was too young than his brother.
He was young to his brother.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 1' i.e. He was younger than his brother is the correct version.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The original sentence "He was youngest than his brother." is incorrect because it improperly uses "youngest" in a comparative context.

• The correct comparative form when comparing two entities is "younger" not "youngest," which is used for superlative comparisons among three or more entities.

• The preposition "than" is correctly used in comparisons, making "younger than" the appropriate phrase to use.

• The correct sentence structure for comparing the age of two people is "Subject + was + younger than + object."

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Correct sentence: *He was younger than his brother.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• "He was youngest to his brother." - This option is incorrect because "youngest" is a superlative form and "to" is not the correct preposition for comparison in this context.

• "He was too young than his brother." - This option is grammatically incorrect because "too" is not used in standard comparative structures, and "than" is misused here.

• "He was young to his brother." - This option lacks a comparative form and incorrectly uses the preposition "to" for comparison.
</ul

questions.question:
Select the option that correctly expresses the following sentence in active voice.

This was talked about in the meeting by the officers.

options.text: The officers were talking about in the meeting.
The officers talked about this in the meeting.
The officers in the meeting had talked about it.
The officers talk about this in the meeting.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 2' i.e. 'The officers talked about this in the meeting' is the sentence rewritten in active voice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The original sentence is in passive voice, indicated by the structure 'was talked about by the officers'.

• To convert to active voice, the subject ('the officers') performs the action of the verb ('talked about').

• The correct active voice construction places the subject at the beginning, followed by the verb and then the object ('this').

• Option 2 correctly rearranges the sentence into active voice without changing its original meaning.

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Correct sentence: *'The officers talked about this in the meeting'*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Option 1 ('The officers were talking about in the meeting') is incorrect because it lacks an object for 'talking about' and does not clearly convert the sentence to active voice.

• Option 3 ('The officers in the meeting had talked about it') changes the tense to past perfect, which is not necessary for converting the given sentence to active voice.

• Option 4 ('The officers talk about this in the meeting') uses the present tense, which changes the meaning of the original sentence that is in the past tense.
</ul

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

From a recent research, __evident is it that a lot more women__ have been opting for professional courses.

options.text: it is evident that more a lot women
it is evidently that a lot more women
it is evident that a lot more women
it is evidence that a lot more women

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 3' i.e. it is evident that a lot more women have been opting for professional courses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The original phrase "*From a recent research, evident is it*" is awkward and incorrectly structured.

• The correct phrase should start with the subject and follow the natural order of English sentences.

• "**It is evident that**" is the correct beginning for the sentence, making it clear and concise.

• The phrase "**a lot more women**" correctly indicates an increase in the number of women choosing professional courses.

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Correct sentence: *From a recent research, it is evident that a lot more women have been opting for professional courses*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• "**it is evidently that**" - This option is incorrect because "evidently" is an adverb and cannot be used in this context where an adjective is required.

• "**it is evidence that**" - This option is incorrect because "evidence" is a noun and the sentence requires the adjective "evident" to describe the clarity of the fact.

• "**it is evident that more a lot women**" - This option is grammatically incorrect and awkwardly phrased. The correct phrase should be "a lot more women."
</ul

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word ‘Bleak’ from the given sentence.

He looked gloomy, frail, broken and slow after the sudden demise of his brother.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Gloomy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Bleak"** refers to an area of land lacking vegetation and exposed to the elements, or to a situation characterized by a lack of hope or encouragement; it often conveys a sense of coldness, emptiness, or despair. (सूना)

 
 
• **Example: **The landscape was bleak in the winter months, with the trees stripped of their leaves and the ground frozen solid.
 
 

 
• **"Gloomy" **refers to something that is dark or poorly lit, often used metaphorically to describe a state of sadness or depression; it mirrors the sense of despair or lack of hope found in something that is bleak. (उदास)

 
 
• **Example: **After hearing the bad news, his mood turned gloomy, and he spent the rest of the day in silence.
 
 

 
• Therefore, the synonym of **'Bleak'** in the given context is **'Gloomy'** as both convey a sense of despair or sadness.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Gloomy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Slow **(धीमा): Lacking in speed, taking a long time to move or happen.
 
 
• **Example:** He was slow to act, which sometimes meant opportunities passed him by.
 
 

 
• **Frail **(कमजोर ): Physically weak or delicate.
 
 
• **Example: **After her illness, she was frail and needed a lot of rest to recover her strength.
 
 

 
• **Sudden** (अचानक): Occurring or done quickly and unexpectedly.
 
 
• **Example:** The sudden storm caught everyone by surprise and caused a lot of damage.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

The students must complete the assignment by Friday.

options.text: The assignment must be completed by the students by Friday.
The assignment will be completed by the students by Friday.
The students will have completed the assignment by Friday.
The assignment must be complete by Friday by the students.

questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The original sentence is in the active voice, and to convert it to the passive voice, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence.

• The modal verb 'must' remains unchanged when transforming the sentence from active to passive voice.

• The phrase 'by the students' is added to indicate who is performing the action in the passive voice.

• The verb 'complete' changes to 'be completed' to form the passive voice structure.

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Correct sentence: *The assignment must be completed by the students by Friday*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Option 2 ('The assignment will be completed by the students by Friday.') incorrectly changes the modal verb 'must' to 'will', altering the meaning and sense of obligation present in the original sentence.

• Option 3 ('The students will have completed the assignment by Friday.') remains in active voice and changes the tense, making it an incorrect transformation.

• Option 4 ('The assignment must be complete by Friday by the students.') is a less preferred construction due to awkward phrasing and redundancy in the placement of 'by the students'.
</ul

questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one - word substitute for the underlined group of words.

Kidney beans were boiled quickly when Nisha added __a substance that speeds up a chemical reaction without being consumed by the reaction itself__.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Catalyst**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Reactant"** refers to a substance that takes part in and undergoes change during a reaction. (प्रतिक्रियाशील पदार्थ)
 
 
• **Example: **Water is a reactant when it reacts with sodium to produce sodium hydroxide and hydrogen gas.
 
 
 
• **"Catalyst"** is a substance that increases the rate of a chemical reaction without itself undergoing any permanent chemical change; it is critical for processes that require a lower activation energy. (उत्प्रेरक)
 
 
• **Example: **Enzymes are biological catalysts that accelerate reactions in the human body.
 
 
 
• **"Enzyme"** is a type of protein that acts as a catalyst in living organisms, speeding up specific biochemical reactions. (एंजाइम)
 
 
• **Example: **The enzyme amylase helps in the breakdown of starch into sugars in the digestive system.
 
 
 
• **"Solute"** is a substance dissolved in another substance, known as the solvent, to form a solution. (विलेय)
 
 
• **Example: **Salt is a solute that dissolves in water, the solvent, to form a saline solution.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the substance that speeds up a chemical reaction without being consumed by the reaction itself is known as a **'Catalyst'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Catalyst**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Reactant** (प्रतिक्रियाशील पदार्थ): A substance participating in a chemical reaction.
 
 
• **Example:** In the reaction between vinegar and baking soda, both are reactants that produce carbon dioxide.
 
 
 
• **Enzyme** (एंजाइम): Biological molecules that significantly speed up the rate of virtually all of the chemical reactions that take place within cells.
 
 
• **Example: **Lactase is an enzyme that helps digest lactose, the sugar in milk.
 
 
 
• **Solute** (विलेय): A substance dissolved in another substance, forming a solution.
 
 
• **Example:** When sugar is added to water, sugar acts as the solute.

questions.question:
RPOQParts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

(O) on a regular basis can improve

(P) engaging in physical activity

(Q) the risk of chronic diseases, and boost mental health

(R) cardiovascular health, reduce
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The correct sequence to form a meaningful sentence is "Engaging in physical activity (P) on a regular basis (O) can improve (O) cardiovascular health, reduce (R) the risk of chronic diseases, and boost mental health (Q)".

• Option 3 (PORQ) correctly arranges these sentence parts to convey a clear, logical message about the benefits of regular physical activity.

• Beginning the sentence with "Engaging in physical activity" sets the subject and action immediately, making it clear what the focus of the sentence is.

• The use of "on a regular basis" following the subject emphasizes the importance of consistency in activity for health benefits.

Therefore, the correct answer is- option 3.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Option 1 (RPOQ) does not logically order the sentence, as it incorrectly places the improvement of cardiovascular health before the mention of engaging in physical activity.

• Option 2 (PROQ) disrupts the logical flow by positioning the reduction of risk before explaining what action leads to these health benefits.

• Option 4 (OQRP) also does not make sense as it starts with the effect before mentioning the cause, which is engaging in physical activity.

• Correct sequencing is crucial for clarity and coherence in sentence construction, as demonstrated by the correct answer.
</ul

questions.question:

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

When I was in 5th grade, / I use to / ride on my / red bicycle.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 2' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The error in the sentence is in the phrase "I use to". The correct expression should be "I used to" when referring to habits or repeated actions in the past.

• The phrase "used to" is a modal verb phrase that indicates past habits or states. It is always followed by the base form of a verb.

• The error involves the incorrect use of the verb tense. The past tense "used" is needed to correctly form the expression.

• Correcting "I use to" to "I used to" resolves the grammatical error, making the sentence reflect a past habit accurately.

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Correct sentence: *"When I was in 5th grade, I used to ride on my red bicycle."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• "When I was in 5th grade," is a time clause that correctly sets the scene in the past with no errors.

• "ride on my" is correctly used, indicating the action of riding something, in this case, a bicycle.

• "red bicycle" correctly describes the object of the sentence with an adjective-noun combination and contains no grammatical errors.

questions.question:

The manager was punished for his negligence in work.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Bid defiance"** means to openly resist or refuse to obey. (अवज्ञा करना)

 
 
• **Example: **The rebel leader bid defiance to the new laws imposed by the government.
 
 

 
• **"Burn one’s boats"** signifies taking an action which makes it impossible to return to the previous situation; a point of no return. (नावों को जलाना - वापसी का कोई मार्ग न छोड़ना)

 
 
• **Example: **By quitting his job and moving to another country, he has truly burned his boats.
 
 

 
• **"Bolt from the blue"** refers to something happening completely unexpectedly, similar to a sudden and unforeseen lightning strike from a clear sky. (आकस्मिक और अप्रत्याशित)

 
 
• **Example: **The sudden resignation of the CEO was a bolt from the blue for the company.
 
 

 
• **"Bring to book"** means to punish someone or make them accountable for their actions. (किसी को उसके कार्यों के लिए दंडित करना या जवाबदेह बनाना)

 
 
• **Example: **The fraudulent investor was finally brought to book after years of illegal activities.
 
 

 
• Hence, relating to the statement about the manager being punished for his negligence, the most appropriate idiom is **"Bring to book."**

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4**.
